title: Tenali Raman Tale 124

full_text:
A celebrated archery master from the northern borders, Drona Sen, arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, boasting that none in the southern empire possessed true mastery of the bow.
He challenged the court archers:
'I can split an apple on a boy’s head at one hundred paces!
I challenge any courtier to shoot an arrow through a suspended iron ring at fifty paces while completely blindfolded!'

The royal archers failed, missing the ring completely.
King Krishnadevaraya turned to Tenali Raman:
'Tenali, canst thou shoot an arrow through the ring while blindfolded?'

Tenali smiled: 'Maharaj, I am a poet, not a warrior. But the mind has eyes that see clearer than physical vision. I accept the challenge!'

Tenali asked that the iron ring be suspended from a rope in the center of the archery range.
He tied a small brass bell to the top of the iron ring.
Tenali then tied a thick black silk cloth over his own eyes, ensuring total blindness.
He took up a royal recurve bow and notched a feathered arrow.

Tenali said: 'Let the wind blow, or let a courtier strike the brass bell once!'
A courtier gently tapped the bell: *‘TING!’*

The clear, ringing tone echoed across the silent courtyard.
Tenali stood motionless for three seconds, his ears attuned to the vibration, calculating the distance, the angle, and the height of the sound with complete, meditative concentration.
He drew the bowstring taut to his cheek, breathed out smoothly, and released the arrow:
*TWANG!*

The arrow whistled through the air!
*CLINK-THWACK!*
The arrow passed cleanly through the center of the suspended iron ring, striking the center of the wooden target post behind it with flawless accuracy!

The entire court erupted in thunderous, deafening cheers!
The northern archery master took off his hat, bowed low, and confessed:
'Tenali Raman, thou hast mastered the ancient secret of *Shabdavedhi*—striking a target purely by sound! Thou art a master of focus!'

The King embraced Tenali: 'Tenali, how didst thou shoot so accurately without eyes?'
Tenali smiled gently:
'Maharaj, physical eyes are easily distracted by the crowd, the flags, and self-doubt.
When the eyes are closed in calm discipline, the mind hears truth without distortion.
A clear mind sees through the ears and strikes true every time!'
moral: True vision is not merely in the eyes, but in the focused discipline of the concentrated mind.
